acceptance: `evolve ci watch --sha S` with a fake fetcher returns 0 on success and 1 on failure (red: unknown subcommand "watch")
`--tag vX.Y.Z` waits for both the required and the release workflows
A red PR run files no inbox item; a red main SHA files one fix-forward item
fix: Add `evolve ci watch (--sha S | --pr N | --tag T) [--workflow W]... [--cycle N]` over ciwatch.Watch with the gh fetcher. It waits for the named workflows to complete (default: the required workflow; a tag adds the release workflow) and prints each conclusion; on red it prints the `ci classify` result. It files the fix-forward item only when watching main or a tag (--cycle names the cycle in it), never for a PR. Exit 0 green, 1 red, 2 on gh I/O or timeout (the policy ci_watch timeout). Point the /commit and /evo:publish skills and runtime-reference.md at it.
source: console, 2026-09-30, core-function CLI inventory (operator request: a CLI request for each core function)
summary: ciwatch.Watch polls a SHA's required CI run and, on red, files a fix-forward inbox item (internal/ciwatch/ciwatch.go:92), but only ACS predicates import it. The /commit skill watches CI with `gh run watch` or `gh pr checks --watch` (skills/commit/SKILL.md:38). /evo:publish watches a tag's required.yml and release.yml with `gh run watch` (skills/publish/SKILL.md:56-57). The release pipeline itself prints 'GitHub CI is NOT verified by this pipeline' (internal/releasepipeline/release_run.go:328).
title: Watching CI for a pushed commit, PR or release tag is `gh run watch` by hand, and ciwatch.Watch has no production caller; add `evolve ci watch`
